name: Orforglipron

track.title: Lab & animal
track.line: Not active in rats or mice; no rodent tumors

what.text: Orforglipron is a GLP-1 receptor agonist taken as a daily tablet. Unlike semaglutide, liraglutide and tirzepatide, it is not a peptide: it is a small, man-made molecule. It is made by Eli Lilly and sold in the US as Foundayo.

src.label: Wharton et al., ATTAIN-1, N Engl J Med

what.text: The label says it binds to and switches on the human GLP-1 receptor, lowers food intake, likely by lowering appetite, and slows stomach emptying. In animal studies it reached brain areas that control appetite. The label says it is not active in rats or mice and did not cause tumors in rodents.
In the US it is approved only for weight management. Using it for type 2 diabetes alone is off-label in the US, though the UK has authorised it for type 2 diabetes.

src.label: MHRA: UK first in Europe to authorise orforglipron

research.text: Orforglipron has been tested in large randomized trials paid for by Eli Lilly: the ATTAIN program for weight and the ACHIEVE program for type 2 diabetes. The main ones are listed below as they were run. The trials used a capsule; the label lists the matching tablet doses (for example, 36 mg capsule equals 17.2 mg tablet).

research.title: ATTAIN-1: weight in adults without diabetes

facts.v: Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled
3,127 adults with obesity, or overweight with a weight-related condition; no diabetes; 64% women
daily orforglipron 6, 12 or 36 mg (capsule), or placebo, with diet and activity advice
72 weeks
percent change in body weight

research.found: Weight changed by -7.5% (6 mg), -8.4% (12 mg) and -11.2% (36 mg), versus -2.1% on placebo. 5.3% to 10.3% on orforglipron and 2.7% on placebo stopped because of side effects. The most common were stomach and bowel effects, mostly mild to moderate. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05869903.

src.label: Wharton et al., ATTAIN-1, N Engl J Med

research.text: ATTAIN-2, in 1,613 adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes, is the second trial behind the US approval. The label reports weight changes of -5.1%, -7.0% and -9.6% on the three tablet doses, versus -2.5% on placebo, at 72 weeks.

research.title: ACHIEVE-1: early type 2 diabetes

facts.v: Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled
559 adults with type 2 diabetes on diet and exercise only, HbA1c 7.0% to 9.5%
daily orforglipron 3, 12 or 36 mg, or placebo
40 weeks
change in HbA1c (long-term blood sugar)

research.found: HbA1c fell by 1.24 to 1.48 points on orforglipron and 0.41 on placebo. Weight changed by -4.5% to -7.6% versus -1.7%. No severe low blood sugar was reported. 4.4% to 7.8% on orforglipron and 1.4% on placebo stopped because of side effects. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05971940.

src.label: Rosenstock et al., ACHIEVE-1, N Engl J Med

research.title: ACHIEVE-3: versus oral semaglutide in type 2 diabetes

facts.v: Phase 3, randomized, open-label, active-controlled
1,698 adults with type 2 diabetes on metformin, HbA1c 7.0% to 10.5%
daily orforglipron 12 or 36 mg, or oral semaglutide 7 or 14 mg
52 weeks
change in HbA1c

research.found: HbA1c fell by 1.71 and 1.91 points on orforglipron and 1.23 and 1.47 on semaglutide. Stomach and bowel effects affected about 58% to 59% on orforglipron and 37% to 45% on semaglutide. 9% to 10% on orforglipron and 4% to 5% on semaglutide stopped because of side effects. Pulse rose more on orforglipron (3.7 to 4.7 beats per minute). ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06045221.

src.label: ACHIEVE-3, orforglipron vs oral semaglutide, Lancet

research.title: ACHIEVE-4: heart safety in type 2 diabetes

facts.v: Phase 3, randomized, open-label, event-driven, versus insulin glargine
2,749 adults with type 2 diabetes, overweight or obesity, and heart or kidney disease; mean age 63
daily orforglipron (up to 36 mg capsule) or daily insulin glargine injections
median follow-up 2 years
heart-related death, heart attack, stroke or hospital stay for unstable angina, counted together

research.found: The combined outcome happened in 4.2% on orforglipron and 5.0% on insulin glargine (hazard ratio 0.84), meeting the trial’s safety goal. Stomach and bowel effects affected 62.1% and 14.2%. Serious low blood sugar affected 6.8% and 19.2%. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05803421.

src.label: ACHIEVE-4, heart safety vs insulin glargine, Lancet

us.text: Orforglipron is FDA approved as Foundayo tablets, since April 1, 2026, for weight management in adults. It is not approved in the US for type 2 diabetes. As of November 1, 2026.

items.text: approved, with a reduced-calorie diet and more physical activity, to reduce excess body weight and keep it off in adults with obesity, or overweight with at least one weight-related condition. FDA classed it as a new molecular entity. A labeling supplement was approved in August 2026.
use for type 2 diabetes alone, or in children, is off-label in the US.
compounded drugs are not FDA approved. FDA does not review their safety, effectiveness or quality before they are sold.

us.text: Foundayo is the FDA-approved orforglipron product. Any compounded or "research" orforglipron is not FDA approved.

world.lead: Orforglipron is approved in the US (weight) and the UK (weight and type 2 diabetes). In the EU, EMA’s committee adopted a positive opinion, but the final decision was not found. It is not prohibited in sport.

after.title: Sport
after.text: Orforglipron is not named on the WADA 2026 Prohibited List or the 2027 Monitoring Program. USADA says GLP-1 medicines are not prohibited in sport and need no therapeutic use exemption. Because orforglipron is approved, the List’s S0 class for unapproved drugs does not apply.

src.label: USADA: Weight loss drugs, what athletes need to know about GLP-1s

side.text: The Foundayo label has a boxed warning, FDA’s strongest kind, about thyroid C-cell tumors, as other GLP-1 drugs do. The most common side effects are stomach and bowel effects.

items.text: other GLP-1 drugs caused thyroid C-cell tumors in rats and mice. Orforglipron is not active in rodents and did not cause them, but the label says the human relevance is unknown. People with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid cancer, or with MEN 2 syndrome, must not use it.
has been seen with GLP-1 drugs, including Foundayo.
stomach and bowel side effects affected 60% to 69% on Foundayo and 37% on placebo in the weight trials; 4% of those affected had severe effects. Up to 6% stopped because of them.
gallstones in 1% on orforglipron and 0.7% on placebo; acute gallbladder inflammation in 0.4% and 0.3%.

items.lead: Kidney injury, low blood sugar, allergy:
items.text: the label warns of kidney injury from dehydration, low blood sugar when used with insulin or drugs that raise insulin, and serious allergic reactions.
not studied in people with eye disease needing urgent treatment.
stomach contents entering the lungs during anesthesia has been reported with GLP-1 drugs.
reported more often in women (7%) than men (0.9%) on Foundayo.
the label advises people on birth-control pills to switch or add a barrier method for 30 days after starting and after each dose increase, and to stop Foundayo when pregnancy is recognized.
nausea, constipation, diarrhea, vomiting, indigestion, belly pain, headache, bloating, tiredness, burping, acid reflux, gas and hair loss.
